sheet-number.purpose: The red number above every sheet title. 3rem below 997px.

display.purpose: The sheet title and the contents-page name. 2.5rem below 997px. Runs to the 46rem sheet width and never breaks inside a word.

display-api.purpose: Identifier titles on API sheets, a step smaller so they never break: 2.25rem below 997px, 1.5rem at 640px and below.

headline.purpose: Numbered section headings; route and Conventions headings on the contents page.

masthead.purpose: The name beside the brand bar.

lede.purpose: The one-paragraph statement on the contents page.

body.purpose: Prose at a 38rem measure, about 66 characters. 1rem is 17px.

rail.purpose: Rail entries, masthead links, tables, tab labels.

small.purpose: On-page contents, captions, colophon, tagline, dropdown items.

label.purpose: Sentence-case group labels in Mute: book heads, On this page, colophon column titles.

code.purpose: Listings and inline code. Ligatures off.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--zm-ease), an ease-out, for every state change and for the plate's wake.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: State changes that ease: colour, background, opacity, and the rail caret's rotation. Hover on a link or a pager rule changes thickness at once, in ink.

motion.name: duration-wake
motion.purpose: Plate 1's trailing legs drawing aft once on load, the single authored movement. Removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: stagger-wake
motion.purpose: Delay per strip edge counted outward from the root, so the wake leaves root first.

narrative.overview:
The documentation is built as a 1970s federal graphics standards manual. Every page is a numbered sheet on one grid, and the sheet number is how a reader finds, cites, and returns to it. A bright white sheet sits beside a cool grey rail, the ink is near black, and one standards red is spent on numbers and place marks. One grotesque, Public Sans, sets everything except code and mathematics.

The frame commits hard and the reading column stays calm. That split is a decision, not an accident: the maintainer called the first, quieter sketches bland and then chose this direction, so the masthead rule, the rail, the red place mark, and the large sheet number are loud on purpose, while prose, listings, equations, and tables are set plainly at a fixed measure for an engineer reading in the middle of work. Light is the default sheet. Dark is the same sheet after hours, token for token, and is never designed separately.

This is a research library's reference. It does not read as a marketing site, as the stock Docusaurus template, or as the near-black, glowing-cyan theme it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Every sheet is numbered, and the rail, the head of the sheet, and the pager print the same number.
One datum edge runs down the sheet; text registers to it and numbers hang in the gutter to its left.
Structure comes from rules, not boxes. Corners are square and nothing casts a shadow.
One red, only on sheet numbers, place marks, the brand bar, and the data ink of Plate 1. Hover and focus are said in ink.
One grotesque in two registers: light at display size, regular to bold for text, with tabular numerals throughout.
Motion answers state changes only; Plate 1's wake is the single authored movement.

rules.name: The Standards Red Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on sheet numbers (above the title, in the pager, in the route lists), place marks (the rail's number cell, the square beside the section in view, the rule under the current book), the brand bar, and the keyed bound vortices of Plate 1. It is never a syntax colour, never a note or warning colour, never a hover or focus colour, and never decoration. The theme's own primary variable (`--ifm-color-primary`) is set to ink, so any stock state the build has not restyled falls back to ink rather than red.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A place mark always changes something besides hue: the current rail row also turns sheet white and bold, the current contents entry and the current book turn bold. Hover follows the same thought from the other side: it changes weight of line, not hue.

rules.name: The Same Sheet Rule
rules.body: Light is the default and dark is its variant. Every colour is a `--zm-*` token redefined once for dark; no component carries a colour of its own for either theme, except the listing inks, which are set as a pair of themes in the site config.

rules.name: The One Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Public Sans sets every word that is not code or mathematics, including labels on listings and plates. Source Code Pro never sets prose, navigation, or labels.

rules.name: The Light At Size Rule
rules.body: Weight 300 is reserved for the sheet number, the sheet title, and the contents-page name. Nothing else is lighter than 400. The only light type below 2.25rem is an API sheet's identifier title on a sheet 640px or narrower, which shrinks so that it never breaks.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case at normal tracking. The one exception in the build is a note's heading, which is 700, uppercase, tracked 0.04em.

rules.name: The Datum Rule
rules.body: Every block on a sheet starts on the one edge right of the datum line. Nothing is centred, and the only indents from it are list items, a display equation (2rem), and quoted text (1.75rem).

rules.name: The 66-Character Rule
rules.body: Prose holds 38rem at every width. A wider element is a sheet title, a listing, a table, or a plate, never a paragraph.

rules.name: The No-Zero Rule
rules.body: Sections and sheets count from 1: sections are 1, 2, 3 and their sheets 1.1, 1.2. The API reference book is lettered, A1, A2.1. The contents page carries no sheet number.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No shadows and no glows, at rest or in any state. Separation is a change of ground or a rule.

rules.name: The Ruled Block Rule
rules.body: A block opens with a 2px ink rule and, if it closes, closes with a hair. Content is never enclosed on four sides; a full border belongs only to a small control floating over the sheet.

dos: Do number every new sheet by its place in the rail, counting from 1, and print that same number in the rail, above the title, and in the pager.
Do start every block on the content edge right of the datum, hold prose to 38rem, and let only listings, tables, and plates run wider.
Do open a block with a 2px ink rule and close it with a 1px hair; keep every corner square.
Do pair every red place mark with a second cue: a change of weight or of ground.
Do say hover in ink: thicken the underline or the rule, or darken the ground.
Do take every colour from a `--zm-*` token so the dark sheet follows without a second design.
Do set keywords in heavier ink and keep listings to green strings, blue names, and amber literals.
Do label things in the text face, in sentence case, in Mute: listing languages, group heads, plate annotations.
Do keep state changes to 160ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't put red on anything but sheet numbers, place marks, the brand bar, and a plate's data ink. It stays out of syntax colours, notes, warnings, and hover and focus states.
Don't start any numbering at 0, and don't give the contents page a sheet number.
Don't round a corner, cast a shadow, or add a glow.
Don't enclose content in a four-sided box or a card. A full border belongs only to a small control floating over the sheet.
Don't colour-code notes by kind. A warning is ruled and set in Ink like any other note.
Don't add a second text face, and don't set prose, navigation, or labels in Source Code Pro.
Don't use weight 300 for anything but the sheet number and the title.
Don't break a title inside a word; set an identifier title smaller instead.
Don't italicise anything in a listing; the code face ships upright only.
Don't make dark the default or give it colours of its own outside the tokens.
Don't animate anything that is not a change of state. Plate 1's wake is the one authored movement.
Don't let a page read as marketing: no slogan hero, no feature cards, and nothing of the stock template or the earlier near-black, glowing-cyan theme.
